_readme: Curated rework techniques. The voice assistant may only choose and adapt these entries; it may not invent advice. Hardware team: edit freely, keep ids stable, and set reviewed to true once an entry has been checked. Issue types: flipped, missing, bridged, lifted_lead, insufficient_solder, excess_solder, cold_joint, tombstoned, misaligned, wrong_part, other. tips: one line of placement guidance per package family, shown under the build screen.

entries.title: Add flux before any rework
steps: Apply a small amount of flux (pen or gel) directly on the joint you are fixing.
Clean the iron tip on the sponge or brass wool and add a tiny bit of fresh solder to it.
Touch the joint for 2–3 seconds, then lift straight off.
entries.check: The joint should look smooth and shiny, with solder flowing onto both the pad and the lead.

entries.title: Remove a solder bridge with braid
steps: Add flux to the bridge.
Lay clean solder braid (desoldering wick) across the bridge.
Press the iron on top of the braid for 2–3 seconds until the solder wicks in.
Lift the braid and the iron away together, so the braid does not stick to the pads.
Cut off the used end of the braid before the next try.
entries.check: Look along the gap between the pins under magnification: you should see board between them. Then use the multimeter in continuity mode between the two pins; it should not beep, unless the schematic connects them.

entries.title: Clear a fine-pitch bridge by dragging the iron
steps: Add plenty of flux along the row of pins.
With a clean, lightly tinned tip, drag slowly along the pins, away from the chip body.
If the bridge stays, use solder braid instead.
entries.check: Each pin should have its own fillet with a visible gap to the next pin. Confirm with a continuity test between neighbouring pins.

entries.title: Reflow a dull, cracked or thin joint
steps: Add flux to the joint.
Heat the pad and the lead together, not just the solder.
Feed a little solder into the point where pad and lead meet, then remove the solder, then the iron.
entries.check: The fillet should be concave and shiny, and should cover the pad up the side of the lead.

entries.title: Re-seat a lifted leg
steps: Add flux to the lifted leg and its pad.
Hold the leg down gently with the tweezer tip.
Heat the pad and leg together and add a little solder; keep holding until the solder sets.
entries.check: The leg should sit flat on the pad with solder visible along its foot. Nudge the part gently with the tweezers; nothing should move.

entries.title: Remove a two-terminal part (to flip or replace it)
steps: Add flux and fresh solder to both ends of the part.
Heat the ends quickly in turn (or use two irons or tweezer irons) until both are molten at once.
Slide the part off with the tweezers; do not pull up on a pad.
Clean the pads with braid, then place the part again the right way round.
entries.check: Before re-soldering, check the pads are flat and intact. After, re-check orientation against the board's marking.

entries.title: Remove a chip placed the wrong way
steps: Stop and confirm the orientation problem against the board's pin-1 mark before removing anything.
Add flux to every pin. Use a hot-air station if available; otherwise flood each row with solder so it stays molten while you heat it.
When all pins are molten, lift the chip straight up with tweezers. Do not lever it.
Clean every pad with braid and flux before placing the chip again.
entries.check: All pads flat and separate, no lifted pads. Re-place with pin 1 matching the board mark, then inspect every pin for bridges.
entries.caution: Pads lift easily when overheated. If you are unsure, ask a TA before removing a chip.

entries.title: Fix a tombstoned part
steps: Add flux to the raised end and its pad.
Heat the soldered end, and while it is molten push the part down flat with the tweezers.
Solder the raised end to its pad, then reflow the first end briefly.
entries.check: Both ends should sit flat on their pads with similar fillets.

entries.title: Re-align a part that is off its pads
steps: Add flux to the joints.
Reheat one end or one row while gently nudging the part into position with the tweezers.
Repeat on the other side, then reflow every joint once.
entries.check: Each lead or end sits on the middle of its pad with no lead touching a neighbouring pad.

entries.title: Place a missing part
steps: Clean the pads with braid if old solder is left on them.
Tin one pad with a small amount of solder.
Hold the part with tweezers, reheat the tinned pad and slide the part in. Remove the iron, then let go.
Solder the other end, then reflow the first end.
entries.check: Part centred on the pads, orientation correct, both joints shiny.

tips.chip2: Tin one pad, slide the part in with tweezers, then solder the other end.
tips.soic: Tack two opposite corner pins, check every pin sits on its pad, then solder the rest.
tips.sot23: Tack the single pin, check the other two sit on their pads, then solder them.
tips.sot223: Tack one leg, check alignment, solder the legs, then the tab.
tips.qfn: Align the corner mark, then reflow with hot air; pads are underneath.
tips.header: Push it in from the top, solder one pin, check it is straight, then the rest.
tips.switch: Tack one corner pad, press the switch flat, then solder the other pads.
tips.generic: Tack one pad, check alignment, then solder the rest.
